verses.commentary: Ephraim feeds on the wind. Consuming nothing. Pursues the east wind all day. The sirocco, the destructive wind. Multiplies lies and violence. Internal corruption. Makes a treaty with Assyria. Playing both superpowers. Sends olive oil to Egypt. Diplomatic gifts to enemies. Double dealing.

The Lord has a charge against Judah. Not just the north. He will punish Jacob according to his ways. Ancestor and descendants united. Repay him according to his deeds. Consequences measured to actions.

In the womb he grasped his brother's heel. Jacob's birth story (Genesis 25:26). As a man he struggled with God. The wrestling at Peniel (Genesis 32:24-28). The ancestor's character defines the nation.

He struggled with the angel and overcame him. Jacob prevailed. He wept and begged for his favor. But also pleaded. He found him at Bethel. The ladder vision (Genesis 28). And talked with him there. Encounter with God in the ancestor's life.
The Lord God Almighty. Full title. The Lord is his name. Covenant name revealed. The ancestor's God is still available.
But you must return to your God. The call to the descendants. Maintain love and justice. The ethical requirements. Wait for your God always. Patient expectation. What Jacob found, they can find.
The merchant uses dishonest scales. Fraudulent commerce. Loves to defraud. Enjoys cheating. The word for merchant is literally Canaan. They have become what they displaced.

Ephraim boasts: I am very rich! Self-congratulation. I have become wealthy. Success celebrated. With all my wealth they will not find in me any iniquity or sin. Wealth as proof of innocence. Prosperity theology.

I have been the Lord your God since Egypt. The old relationship. I will make you live in tents again. Return to wilderness simplicity. As in the days of your appointed festivals. The Feast of Tabernacles recaptured. Stripping away to basics.
I spoke to the prophets. God's communication history. Gave them many visions. Revelation abundant. Told parables through them. Various methods of speaking. God has not been silent.

Is Gilead wicked? Rhetorical question expecting yes. Its people are worthless! Confirmed. Do they sacrifice bulls in Gilgal? Improper sacrifice at improper places. Their altars will be like piles of stones. Ruined, collapsed, mere rubble.
Jacob fled to the country of Aram. The ancestor's exile (Genesis 28-31). Israel served to get a wife. Labor for Rachel. To pay for her he tended sheep. Humble work for love.
The Lord used a prophet to bring Israel up from Egypt. Moses. By a prophet he cared for him. Prophetic leadership in the wilderness. God's consistent method.
But Ephraim has aroused his bitter anger. Provocation to wrath. His Lord will leave on him the guilt of his bloodshed. No forgiveness without repentance. Repay him for his contempt. Insult returned.
